tasks.title: Framework ownership and support contract
tasks.contract: Each platform capability has one framework owner, explicit unsupported behavior, and declared host coverage.

tasks.title: Scoped host service composition
tasks.contract: Applications receive semantic host services through scoped composition; OS-specific implementations remain in framework backends.

tasks.title: SDK surface and no-new-leaks enforcement
tasks.contract: The application SDK exposes semantic contracts without leaking native APIs, target conditionals, or backend features into app packages.

tasks.title: Target and feature dependency gates
tasks.contract: Target and feature resolution produces valid platform graphs without unintended native dependency leakage.

tasks.title: Known folders, locale and time zones
tasks.contract: Known folders, locale, and time-zone data come from host providers with explicit unavailable states and stable semantic values.

tasks.title: Private locations and state migration
tasks.contract: Private data, state, configuration, cache, and runtime locations preserve isolation and remain discoverable across upgrades.

tasks.title: Host architecture and executable capability selection
tasks.contract: Package selection uses the executable host architecture and usable instruction set without treating unknown architecture as a default.

tasks.title: Private and durable filesystem primitives
tasks.contract: Private filesystem operations preserve no-follow, ownership, atomic publication, durability, and cleanup semantics across supported hosts.

tasks.title: Cross-process locks and process incarnation
tasks.contract: Cross-process exclusion binds locks and leases to process incarnation so stale owners cannot retain or regain authority.

tasks.title: Migrate durable storage consumers
tasks.contract: Durable storage consumers retain existing on-disk formats while using framework-owned storage, recovery, and cleanup primitives.

tasks.title: Owned authenticated local connections
tasks.contract: Local connections authenticate both endpoints, scope authority to the intended service, and reject stale or inherited handles.

tasks.title: Migrate brokers and typed service clients
tasks.contract: Brokers and service clients use typed framework transports while preserving protocol authorization and bounded framing.

tasks.title: Control and session activity transport
tasks.contract: Control and session activity use one authenticated transport with stable command, cancellation, and lifecycle semantics.

tasks.title: Managed process trees and tools
tasks.contract: Managed tools have bounded output, cancellation, descendant cleanup, and explicit failure when required lifetime control is unavailable.

tasks.title: Terminal session service
tasks.contract: Terminal sessions preserve PTY resize, input, output, exit, and confinement semantics through a host-owned service.

tasks.title: Host-native choose, open and reveal
tasks.contract: Choose, open, and reveal requests preserve grants, cancellation, and error distinctions through native host providers.

tasks.title: Application discovery, launch and semantic shortcuts
tasks.contract: Application discovery and launch use stable identities, authorized working context, and semantic shortcuts without shell-string handoff.

tasks.title: Trash and owned drag artifacts
tasks.contract: Trash and drag artifacts retain native identity and ownership, and temporary artifacts are released exactly once.

tasks.title: Credential custody and scoped secrets
tasks.contract: Secrets remain scoped to the intended app, profile, and origin; locked or denied custody never silently falls back.

tasks.title: Host trust and SSH identity discovery
tasks.contract: Host trust and SSH identity discovery preserve native trust policy, private-file protections, and explicit changed-key approval.

tasks.title: Read-only system observations
tasks.contract: System observations distinguish unavailable data from false or empty values and bind process actions to verified incarnation.

tasks.title: Hardware and desktop service providers
tasks.contract: Hardware and desktop services expose owned sessions with native authorization, revocation, and hotplug behavior.

tasks.title: Firewall and VPN operations
tasks.contract: Firewall and VPN operations use fixed semantic operations with explicit privilege, availability, and rollback outcomes.

tasks.title: Package, container, model and enrollment administration
tasks.contract: Administrative package, container, model, and enrollment operations use bounded helpers and explicit caller authority.

tasks.title: Portable media and native-frame contract
tasks.contract: Media contracts use portable sample and frame semantics while native resource handles remain opaque and backend-owned.

tasks.title: Capture and device sessions
tasks.contract: Capture sessions are consent-bound, revocable, and own their camera, microphone, or screen resources for their full lifetime.

tasks.title: Playback, audio graphs and desktop media sessions
tasks.contract: Playback and desktop media sessions preserve seek, gain, device, and now-playing behavior through one semantic interface.

tasks.title: Decode, waveform and export jobs
tasks.contract: Decode, waveform, and export jobs are bounded, cancellable, and retain media timing and output fidelity.

tasks.title: Browser engine, private instances and bundle ownership
tasks.contract: The browser engine, private instances, helper IPC, sandbox, and installed bundle form one framework-owned backend.

tasks.title: One native PDF engine owner
tasks.contract: PDF rendering and text extraction use one native engine owner with bounded documents and explicit unavailable behavior.

tasks.title: Speech, OCR, spellcheck and model assets
tasks.contract: Speech, OCR, spellcheck, and model assets use shared providers with declared availability and owned model data.

tasks.title: Filesystem semantics independent of FUSE
tasks.contract: Filesystem semantics use stable resource identity, checked operations, and authorization independent of any FUSE projection.

tasks.title: App workspace clients and hydration
tasks.contract: Workspace clients distinguish projected metadata from hydrated content and preserve identity, cursor, and access-control checks.

tasks.title: Native projections and filesystem service lifecycle
tasks.contract: Native projections have an authenticated lifecycle, bounded recovery, and no framework dependency on application code.

tasks.title: Imager profile codec and authorized media service
tasks.contract: Imager media operations use an authorized service and a stable profile codec shared by build and runtime consumers.

tasks.title: Imager private cache and migration storage
tasks.contract: Imager caches and migrations preserve private ownership, verified content, durable receipts, and native names.

tasks.title: Imager connected-folder transaction closure
tasks.contract: Connected-folder changes use witnessed transactions, leases, idempotent recovery, and durable endpoint identity.

tasks.title: Desktop and Bootc installation providers
tasks.contract: Desktop and Bootc installation use explicit host providers with authenticated artifacts and rollback-aware state.

tasks.title: Sandbox and compositor backend boundaries
tasks.contract: Sandbox and compositor backends retain confinement, resource ownership, and explicit capability availability.

tasks.title: Login, boot, update and privileged deployment
tasks.contract: Login, boot, update, and privileged deployment preserve authenticated state transitions and recoverable publication.

tasks.title: Compatibility, VM and projection backends
tasks.contract: Compatibility, VM, and projection backends expose stable semantic boundaries without leaking guest or helper internals.

tasks.title: Portable and native verification suites
tasks.contract: Portable contract tests run independently of native backend tests, which exercise real behavior only on capable hosts.

tasks.title: Framework distribution and host tooling
tasks.contract: Framework distribution includes the required host tools and assets with stable installed paths and target-specific packaging.

tasks.title: Closure audit and final support certification
tasks.contract: Release certification requires an owner for each retained finding and satisfaction of the declared support matrix.
